entries.definition: to scatter in different directions
entries.definitionCN: 使散开；驱散（词根 spargere 加前缀 dis-）

entries.definition: in a thinly spread way
entries.definitionCN: 稀疏地（sparse 加副词后缀 -ly）

entries.definition: the state of being thin or few
entries.definitionCN: 稀疏性；稀少

entries.definition: thrown or lying in different places
entries.definitionCN: 分散的；零落的

entries.definition: not dense or crowded
entries.definitionCN: 稀薄的；不密的

entries.definition: too poor to support much growth
entries.definitionCN: 贫瘠的（强调长不出东西，不只是稀少）

normalIntro.en: Sparse keeps the picture of something sprinkled thinly over a surface, with the surface still visible.
normalIntro.cn: sparse 保留着「稀稀地洒在表面上、表面仍然可见」的画面。

normal.en: A sparse population lives in the remote north.
normal.cn: 偏远北方人口稀疏。

normal.en: Sparse vegetation covers the dry plain.
normal.cn: 稀疏的植被覆盖着干旱平原。

normal.en: The report is based on sparse evidence.
normal.cn: 这份报告依据的证据很稀少。

normal.en: Sparsely populated is the common adverb partner.
normal.cn: sparsely populated 是常见搭配，表示人口稀少。

normal.en: Link it to disperse: both come from Latin spargere, to scatter.
normal.cn: 与 disperse 联系：两者都出自拉丁语 spargere（撒开）。

abstract.en: Picture a lawn with three blades of grass and a lot of bare soil.
abstract.cn: 想象草坪上只有三根草和一大片裸露的土。

abstract.en: Imagine a map almost empty except for three tiny dots.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图几乎空白，只剩三个小点。

abstract.en: Think of a handful of rice tossed across a large table.
abstract.cn: 想象把一把米撒在大桌子上，处处是空隙。

examples.en: Traffic was sparse on the mountain road after dark.
examples.cn: 天黑后山路上车辆稀少。

examples.en: Sparse vegetation struggles to hold the soil in place.
examples.cn: 稀疏的植被难以固定土壤。

examples.en: The evidence for the theory remains sparse.
examples.cn: 支持这一理论的证据依然稀少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死怕死」——东西少到让人怕，稀疏得很；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁语词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 spargere（撒、散布）→ 过去分词 sparsus（被撒开的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 sparsus → 英语 sparse，核心义「稀稀地散开」。

sensesIntro.en: Sparse starts from the physical picture of things scattered thinly, then extends to low density, intermittent appearance, thin texture and finally thin content.
sensesIntro.cn: sparse 从「东西稀稀地散开」的实体画面出发，先后扩展到密度低、间断出现、质地稀薄，最后落到内容单薄。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few blades of grass on a wide dry plain.
core.cn: 核心意象：干草原上只有几株草。

branches.en: The literal picture of wide gaps gives the basic adjective.
branches.cn: 间隔很大的实物画面给出最基本的形容词义。

branches.en: People, plants and hair can all be thinly distributed over a surface.
branches.cn: 人口、植物与头发都能稀疏地分布在表面上。

branches.en: Intermittent occurrence is the same picture applied to events in time.
branches.cn: 间断出现是把同一画面用在时间里的事件上。

branches.en: Data and evidence treated as scattered grains give the content sense.
branches.cn: 把数据与证据当作散落的颗粒，就得到了内容义。

branches.en: Whether in space or in argument, what is sparse leaves a lot of empty room.
branches.cn: 无论空间还是论证，稀疏之处都留下大量空白。

intro.en: Sparse is a Latinate adjective, with English sparsely, sparseness and sparsity built around it.
intro.cn: sparse 是拉丁来源的形容词，英语围绕它构成 sparsely、sparseness 与 sparsity。

latinIntro.en: Latin spargere means to scatter, and its participle sparsus means strewn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spargere 意为撒开，其分词 sparsus 意为被撒开的。

items.example: Sparsus is the participle behind sparse.
items.exampleCN: sparsus 是 sparse 背后的分词形式。

items.example: Sparse keeps the participle sense.
items.exampleCN: sparse 保留了分词的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sparsely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 sparsely。

items.example: Sparsely pairs with populated.
items.exampleCN: sparsely 常与 populated 搭配。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms sparseness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 sparseness。

items.example: Sparseness describes the gaps themselves.
items.exampleCN: sparseness 描述的是空隙本身。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms sparsity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 sparsity。

items.example: Sparsity is common in statistics.
items.exampleCN: sparsity 常见于统计领域。

items.example: The prefix dis- gives disperse.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 dis- 构成 disperse。

definition_zh: 痉挛；抽筋；阵发；（情绪或活动）一阵突发；（经济或政治）短暂剧烈波动
definition_en: a sudden uncontrolled tightening of a muscle, or a short burst of strong feeling or activity
core_image: 小腿肌肉忽然自己绷紧抽住，疼得人抓住床沿
scene: 半夜里游泳的人突然小腿抽搐，疼得蜷起身子。A spasm in his calf woke him and made him sit up in pain.
sceneCN: 这里 spasm 是「肌肉痉挛」（第 1 个义项：肌肉不自主地猛收紧）；句意为小腿抽筋使他醒来并痛得坐起；画面里有蜷起的腿、湿毛巾与夜里的床沿。

pos.zh: 名词：痉挛；抽筋；一阵突发

derivatives.zh: 由 spasm 加希腊语词尾 -odes 演变而来，义为「痉挛性的；间歇性的」
由 spasmodic 加 -ally 构成，义为「一阵一阵地；间歇地」
前缀 anti-（抗）加 spasmodic，义为「解痉的」，也作名词指解痉药

senses.title: Sudden involuntary muscle tightening
senses.definition: a sudden, strong and painful tightening of a muscle that you cannot control
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉突然强烈收紧，疼痛且无法自控
senses.example: The runner limped off with a spasm in her thigh.
senses.exampleCN: 那名跑步者大腿抽筋，一瘸一拐地退下场。
senses.why: The Greek root means to draw or pull, and a spasm is the body pulling a muscle tight on its own.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根意为「拉、抽」，spasm 就是身体自作主张把肌肉拉紧的那一下。

senses.title: A short burst of feeling
senses.definition: a brief, intense and uncontrollable surge of emotion or reaction
senses.definitionCN: 短暂、强烈且不由自主的情绪或反应爆发
senses.example: A spasm of jealousy shot through him at the sight of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 一看到那封信，一阵嫉妒猛然袭过他。
senses.why: Emotions grip the body the way a cramp does, so the medical picture easily extends to sudden inner convulsions.
senses.whyCN: 情绪抓住身体的方式正如抽筋，于是医学画面顺势扩展到内心突然的揪紧。

senses.title: A fit of coughing or laughing
senses.definition: a short uncontrollable fit of a bodily action such as coughing, laughing or crying
senses.definitionCN: 咳嗽、大笑、抽泣等躯体动作短促而不可控的一阵发作
senses.example: He doubled over in a spasm of coughing.
senses.exampleCN: 他弯下腰，猛咳了一阵。
senses.why: The body throws itself into a burst of action and then releases, exactly the rhythmic grab and let go of a cramp.
senses.whyCN: 身体猛地投入一阵动作再松开，其节奏与抽筋的一紧一松完全相同。

senses.title: A short burst of activity
senses.titleCN: 活动中一阵短暂的激增
senses.definition: a sudden short spell of intense activity, often in groups or bursts rather than steadily
senses.definitionCN: 突然而短暂的一段高强度活动，常表现为成阵出现而非持续稳定
senses.example: The factory works in spasms rather than at a steady pace.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂是一阵忙一阵闲，而不是匀速运转。
senses.why: Work, growth or effort can tighten and release like a muscle, so activity comes in fits and starts.
senses.whyCN: 工作、增长或用力也会像肌肉一样绷紧又放松，于是活动呈现一阵一阵的样子。

senses.title: An economic or political convulsion
senses.definition: a brief and violent disturbance in markets, trade or politics that soon eases
senses.definitionCN: 市场、贸易或政治中短暂而猛烈的动荡，随后缓和
senses.example: A spasm in the currency market caught small exporters off guard.
senses.exampleCN: 汇率市场的一次剧烈波动让小出口商措手不及。
senses.why: A whole economy can seize up briefly and relax again, which makes a market event look like a body cramping.
senses.whyCN: 整个经济体也会短暂「抽紧」再松开，于是市场事件看起来就像身体痉挛。

intro.en: Spasm comes from Greek spasmos, from span, to draw or pull, and reached English through Latin and French medical texts.
intro.cn: spasm 来自希腊语 spasmos，源于动词 span（拉、抽），经由拉丁语与法语医学文献进入英语。

items.en: Span means to draw, pull or tear, and spasmos means a pulling or a convulsion.
items.cn: span 意为拉、扯，spasmos 意为抽拉或抽搐。

items.en: Hippocratic writers use spasmos for the tightening of muscles in illness.
items.cn: 希波克拉底一派的医者用 spasmos 指疾病中肌肉的紧绷。

items.en: Latin medical writers borrow the term as spasmus.
items.cn: 拉丁语医学作者借入该词，写作 spasmus。

items.en: Old French spasme carries the medical term into western Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 spasme 把这个医学术语带入西欧。

items.en: Spasm enters English first in medical writing and later widens to emotion and business.
items.cn: spasm 先以医学用语进入英语，后来扩展到情绪与商业。

note.en: Spasm shares the Greek pulling root with spasmodic, and sits beside ordinary words for cramps and fits.
note.cn: spasm 与 spasmodic 共享希腊语「拉」的词根，并与一批表示抽筋与发作的常用词相邻。

entries.definition: happening in sudden short bursts
entries.definitionCN: 痉挛性的；间歇性的

entries.definition: relieving muscle cramps
entries.definitionCN: 解痉的

entries.definition: related to stiff or jerky muscle movement
entries.definitionCN: 痉挛性的（医学术语，与 spasm 同出希腊语 span）

entries.definition: a sudden painful tightening of a muscle
entries.definitionCN: 抽筋；痉挛（更口语）

entries.definition: a sudden attack of illness or action
entries.definitionCN: 发作；一阵（动作）

entries.definition: a violent uncontrollable shaking
entries.definitionCN: 惊厥；剧烈抽搐（更严重的医学用语）

normalIntro.en: Spasm keeps the Greek picture of something pulled tight and then released.
normalIntro.cn: spasm 保留着希腊语「被拉紧、再松开」的画面。

normal.en: A muscle spasm can strike at night.
normal.cn: 肌肉痉挛会在夜里突然发生。

normal.en: A spasm of anger passed over his face.
normal.cn: 他脸上一阵暴怒掠过。

normal.en: She shook with a spasm of laughter.
normal.cn: 她笑得一阵发抖。

normal.en: Spasmodic means coming in bursts, from the same root.
normal.cn: spasmodic 意为时断时续，与 spasm 同源。

normal.en: In spasms means in small bursts.
normal.cn: in spasms 表示一阵一阵地。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber band snapped tight between two fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象橡皮筋在两指之间被绷得笔直。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand closing on a stone and then letting go.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手猛地抓住石头又松开。

abstract.en: Think of a traffic light flicking from green to red and back.
abstract.cn: 想象红绿灯突然由绿转红再转回绿。

examples.en: A spasm in his back forced him to lie down.
examples.cn: 背部的一阵痉挛使他不得不躺下。

examples.en: She felt a spasm of guilt when she read the message.
examples.cn: 读到那条消息时，她心头一阵愧疚。

examples.en: The market suffered a brief spasm before recovering.
examples.cn: 市场经历了一次短暂动荡后恢复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撕怕着呢」——肌肉被猛地撕紧，一阵抽筋；这只是谐音联想，与希腊语词源无关。

root: 古希腊语 span（拉、抽）→ spasmos（抽搐）→ 拉丁语 spasmus → 古法语 spasme → 英语 spasm，核心义「猛一拉紧」。

sensesIntro.en: Spasm begins as a muscle pulled tight against the will, then extends to emotional surges, bodily fits, bursts of activity and finally market convulsions.
sensesIntro.cn: spasm 起初指肌肉违背意志地猛收紧，随后扩展到情绪骤起、身体发作、一阵阵活动，最后指市场的剧烈波动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calf muscle that suddenly locks tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：小腿肌肉突然绷紧锁住。

branches.en: The literal muscle sense is the core.
branches.cn: 肌肉字面义是核心。

branches.en: A tightening grip of feeling follows the same image inside.
branches.cn: 内心的情绪也是一下猛然揪紧。

branches.en: Coughing and laughing release in the same grab and let go.
branches.cn: 咳嗽与大笑同样是猛地一抓再松开。

branches.en: Work and markets can tighten and relax like a body.
branches.cn: 工作与金融市场也像身体一样绷紧又放松。

branches.en: Both a cramp and a fit are short, unexpected and hard to control.
branches.cn: 抽筋与发作都短促、突然且难以控制。

intro.en: Spasm is a Greek medical loanword, with English spasmodic, spasmodically and antispasmodic built around it.
intro.cn: spasm 是希腊语医学借词，英语围绕它构成 spasmodic、spasmodically 与 antispasmodic。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek term as spasmus, and later English adjectives were formed on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语以 spasmus 借入这个希腊词，后来英语形容词也在同一词干上构成。

items.example: Spasmos is the Greek source of spasm.
items.exampleCN: spasmos 是 spasm 的希腊语来源。

items.example: The verb span gives the pulling image.
items.exampleCN: 动词 span 提供「拉」的意象。

items.example: Spasm keeps the noun sense.
items.exampleCN: spasm 保留名词含义。

items.example: The ending lies behind spasmodic.
items.exampleCN: 这一结尾见于 spasmodic。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms spasmodic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 spasmodic。

items.example: Spasmodic describes uneven effort.
items.exampleCN: spasmodic 描述忽强忽弱的用力。

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式的副词词尾
items.example: The adverb ends in -ally.
items.exampleCN: 该副词以 -ally 结尾。

items.example: The prefix anti- gives antispasmodic.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 anti- 构成 antispasmodic。

items.example: Antispasmodic names a kind of drug.
items.exampleCN: antispasmodic 指一类药物。

definition_zh: 产卵；鱼卵；产生；催生；大量生成；（游戏或程序）生成对象
definition_en: to produce eggs in water, or to produce a large number of something new
core_image: 溪底水草间挤着一团团透明的鱼卵，每团里都是小黑点
scene: 春天积雪化尽，清冷的溪水涨起来，鱼群顶水而上寻找浅滩。Every spring the salmon swim upstream to spawn in the cold gravel.
sceneCN: 这里 spawn 是「产卵」（第 1 个义项：鱼类把卵产在水中）；句意为鲑鱼每年春季上溯到冰冷的砾石床产卵；画面里有融雪、浅滩、砾石与鱼群。

pos.zh: 动词：产卵；产生；催生；大量生成

derivatives.zh: 由 spawn 加 -er 构成，义为「产卵的鱼」或「生成程序」
由 spawn 加 -ing 构成的动名词，义为「产卵；生成」
由 spawn 加 -less 构成，义为「不产卵的；无子代的」

senses.title: To produce eggs in water
senses.definition: to release eggs into water, especially by fish, frogs or similar animals
senses.definitionCN: 把卵排入水中，尤指鱼类、蛙类等
senses.example: Frogs spawn in the shallow pond each April.
senses.exampleCN: 每年四月青蛙在浅水塘里产卵。
senses.why: The core picture is a mass of eggs poured into water, so the verb names that single act of release.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是一团卵被倾入水中，动词便直接指这一次释放。

senses.title: Fish eggs
senses.definition: the eggs of fish or other aquatic animals, taken as a mass, or the offspring from them
senses.definitionCN: 鱼类等水生动物被看作一团团的卵，或由卵孵化出的后代
senses.example: The stream bed was thick with spawn.
senses.exampleCN: 溪床上密密麻麻都是鱼卵。
senses.why: Once the eggs are the object in view rather than the act, the same word becomes the noun for that cluster.
senses.whyCN: 当被注视的对象从动作变成卵本身，同一个词就成了指那一团的名称。

senses.title: To give rise to something new
senses.definition: to cause something new to come into being, especially in large numbers or over time
senses.definitionCN: 使新事物出现，尤指大量地或随着时间产生
senses.example: The invention spawned a whole new industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发明催生了一个全新的行业。
senses.why: Just as eggs scatter into hundreds of future fish, one cause can throw out many new results.
senses.whyCN: 就像卵散开后会变成成百上千条鱼，一个原因也能抛出许多新结果。

senses.title: To cause a problem or debate
senses.definition: to provoke or give birth to a problem, argument or controversy
senses.definitionCN: 引发或招来问题、争论或争议
senses.example: The report spawned a fierce debate about water use.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告引发了一场关于用水的激烈争论。
senses.why: A controversy can multiply in followers like roe in a stream, so the word takes on a pejorative edge.
senses.whyCN: 争论像溪中鱼卵一样不断增殖，于是这个词带上了一点贬义色彩。

senses.title: To create instances in computing or games
senses.definition: to create an object, character or process, typically many at a time, in software or a game
senses.definitionCN: 在软件或游戏中创建对象、角色或进程，通常一次大量生成
senses.example: The game spawns monsters as soon as you open the door.
senses.exampleCN: 你一开门，游戏就开始生成怪物。
senses.why: New objects appearing in the hundreds repeat the old picture of eggs bursting into life.
senses.whyCN: 数百个新对象同时出现，重现了卵一下爆出生命的老画面。

intro.en: Spawn is probably from Old French espandre, to shed or spread out, itself from Latin expandere to spread, in the sense of roe shed from the body.
intro.cn: spawn 一般认为来自古法语 espandre（流出、铺开），再往前是拉丁语 expandere（展开），取其「卵从体内排出」之意。

items.en: Expandere means to spread out or unfold.
items.cn: expandere 意为展开、铺开。

items.en: Espandre develops the sense of shedding or pouring out, including eggs.
items.cn: 古法语 espandre 发展出「排出、倒出」之义，包括产卵。

items.en: Spawn appears in English meaning the roe of fish.
items.cn: spawn 约在十五世纪进入英语，指鱼卵。

items.en: The verb sense of fish laying eggs is well established.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，动词义「鱼类产卵」已经确立。

items.en: Figurative use for products, problems and digital objects then spreads widely.
items.cn: 随后比喻用法扩展到产品、问题与数字对象。

note.en: Spawn sits with spread and expand in its family, and with everyday words for reproducing and creating.
note.cn: spawn 与 spread、expand 同属「铺开」词族，并与表示繁殖与产生的常用词相邻。

entries.definition: a fish that lays eggs, or a generating program
entries.definitionCN: 产卵的鱼；生成程序

entries.definition: the act of producing eggs
entries.definitionCN: 产卵（动作）

entries.definition: an eating utensil
entries.definitionCN: 勺子（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to produce young animals
entries.definitionCN: 繁殖；繁育（多指动物的整体繁殖行为）

entries.definition: to produce or create something
entries.definitionCN: 产生；生成

entries.definition: to come out of an egg
entries.definitionCN: 孵出（侧重卵变成幼体）

normalIntro.en: Spawn pictures a cloud of eggs leaving a body and filling the water, and every new thing can be born the same way.
normalIntro.cn: spawn 想象一团团卵离开身体铺满溪水，而任何新事物都可以这样出生。

normal.en: Salmon return to spawn in their home river.
normal.cn: 鲑鱼回到出生的河里产卵。

normal.en: New technology spawns new jobs.
normal.cn: 新技术催生新工作。

normal.en: The film spawned three sequels.
normal.cn: 这部电影催生了三部续集。

normal.en: Spawning season is when fish lay their eggs.
normal.cn: spawning season 是鱼类产卵的季节。

normal.en: The base word literally names the eggs as well as the act.
normal.cn: 这个词本身既指动作，也直接指鱼卵本身。

abstract.en: Picture a cloud of dust puffing out from a clap.
abstract.cn: 想象拍手时腾起的一团灰尘。

abstract.en: Imagine one seed turning into a field of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子长成一整片草地。

abstract.en: Think of a video game doorway filling with tiny monsters.
abstract.cn: 想象游戏门口一下涌满小怪物。

examples.en: Many tropical fish spawn shortly after sunset.
examples.cn: 许多热带鱼在日落后不久产卵。

examples.en: The crisis spawned dozens of new regulations.
examples.cn: 这场危机催生了数十条新规定。

examples.en: Each coral colony releases spawn into the current.
examples.cn: 每一个珊瑚群落都把卵排入水流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死破昂」——鱼卵一破，小生命昂着头游出来，便是一次产卵；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 expandere（展开、铺开）→ 古法语 espandre（流出、排出）→ 英语 spawn（鱼卵；产卵）→ 引申为「催生、生成」，核心义「大量铺散而出」。

sensesIntro.en: Spawn first names eggs shed into water, then the act of producing them, then the wider idea of giving rise to many new things at once.
sensesIntro.cn: spawn 先指排入水中的卵，再指产卵这个动作，然后泛化为「一次性催生许多新东西」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cluster of eggs clouding the gravel bed of a stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团团鱼卵铺满溪床的砾石。

branches.en: Spawning as an act is the animal sense.
branches.cn: 作为动作的产卵是动物义项。

branches.en: The eggs themselves become the mass noun.
branches.cn: 卵本身成为指那一团的集合名词。

branches.en: Products and controversies are treated as multiplying offspring.
branches.cn: 产品与争议被当作不断增殖的后代。

branches.en: Digital objects materialise in batches, like eggs hatching.
branches.cn: 数字对象成批出现，像卵在孵化。

branches.en: A spawning fish and a spawning industry both pour out multiples.
branches.cn: 产卵的鱼和催生新事物的行业，都是成倍地抛出东西。

intro.en: Spawn is a word with an uncertain but clearly Romance history, with English spawner, spawning and spawnless around it.
intro.cn: spawn 的词源虽无定论，但显然与罗曼语有关，英语围绕它构成 spawner、spawning 与 spawnless。

latinIntro.en: The likely Latin ancestor is expandere, to spread out, which Old French reshaped as espandre.
latinIntro.cn: 最可能的拉丁语祖词是 expandere（铺开），古法语把它改造成 espandre。

items.example: Expandere probably lies behind spawn.
items.exampleCN: expandere 一般认为在 spawn 背后。

items.example: Espandre carries the shedding sense.
items.exampleCN: espandre 带来「排出」之意。

items.example: Spawn first names the eggs.
items.exampleCN: spawn 最初指鱼卵。

items.example: The verb then names the laying.
items.exampleCN: 动词接着指产卵这个动作。

items.example: The suffix -er forms spawner.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 spawner。

items.example: Spawner also names a generating tool.
items.exampleCN: spawner 也指生成工具。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms spawning.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 spawning。

items.example: Spawning is common in spring.
items.exampleCN: 产卵常见于春季。

items.example: The suffix -less forms spawnless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 spawnless。
